chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from a man from the Banu Hashim, who said:

Four (qualities): whoever possesses them, his Islam will be perfected; and even if he had sins from his head to his feet, truthfulness, bashfulness (modesty), good character, and gratitude would not diminish (his faith/status).
ai.seo_question: What four virtues perfect Islam and compensate for sins according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this chain to highlight that truthfulness (sidq), modesty (haya'), good character (husn al-khuluq), and gratitude (shukr) are the pillars that perfect Islam, effectively offsetting even a lifetime of sins. This reflects the Shia emphasis on ethical conduct (akhlaq) as a means of spiritual purification and divine acceptance, underscoring that inner virtue can compensate for outward transgressions.

en.hubeali:
Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from a man from the Clan of Hashim<sup>as</sup>, he<sup>asws</sup> said, ‘

Four (things), if these are in someone, his Islām would be perfect, and even if he was in sin from his head to his feet, it would not incur him a loss – the truthfulness, and the bashfulness, and the good mannerisms, and the gratefulness’.
en.sarwar: 6. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Ali from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from a man from Banu Hashim who has said the following:

“If four things are found in a person his Islam is perfect, even though he may be fdled with sins from his top to his toes it will not harm him. They consist of Truthfulness, Bashfulness, Good Moral Behavior and Thankfulness.”
